name: Broken Object Level Authorization
summary: An API exposes object-level operations without consistently verifying that the authenticated user is authorized to access the requested object.
description: Broken Object Level Authorization occurs when an application checks that a user is authenticated but fails to verify whether that user is allowed to access or modify the specific object identified by a request.

name: Missing Function Level Authorization
summary: An application exposes privileged operations without enforcing authorization checks for the requested function or endpoint.
description: Missing Function Level Authorization occurs when authenticated users can reach administrative or privileged functionality because the server does not consistently enforce authorization rules for each protected operation.

name: SQL Injection
summary: Application input reaches a database query without safe parameterization or equivalent separation between data and query structure.
description: SQL Injection occurs when untrusted input is incorporated into SQL commands in a way that allows the input to alter the intended query structure.

name: Credential Reuse
summary: Users reuse credentials across services, increasing the impact of credential compromise and automated authentication attempts.
description: Credential reuse becomes a security weakness when passwords or other authentication secrets are reused across multiple services, allowing compromise of one service to increase exposure elsewhere.

name: Weak Session Management
summary: Session handling does not adequately protect authentication state throughout login, use, renewal, and logout.
description: Weak session management can expose authenticated accounts when session identifiers are insufficiently protected, are not rotated appropriately, remain valid longer than necessary, or are not invalidated correctly after sensitive events.

name: API Authorization Bypass
summary: An API endpoint permits access to protected functionality without enforcing the authorization boundary expected for the requesting user.
description: An API authorization bypass occurs when server-side authorization logic can be bypassed because one or more endpoints rely on client-side assumptions, inconsistent policy enforcement, or missing permission checks.
